nodes.summary: The Dedekind zeta function is the Dirichlet series of the number $a_K(n)$ of ideals of norm $n$. These counts are multiplicative. In a quadratic field, at a prime power $p^k$ they are the partial sums of the powers of a sign $\varepsilon_p\in\{-1,0,1\}$, and if $\mathcal O_K$ contains a square root of a non-square integer $d$, then for odd $p\nmid d$ that sign is the Legendre symbol $(d/p)$. nodes.title: Ideal counts in quadratic fields

nodes.summary: Throughout, $q\ge1$, $\chi$ is a Dirichlet character modulo $q$, $\chi_0$ the principal one, and $M=\log q+3$. For $\chi\ne\chi_0$ the $L$-function $L(s,\chi)$ is entire and equals $\sum_{n\ge1}\chi(n)n^{-s}$ for $\mathrm{Re}\,s>1$. Every bound below is explicit, and the value at $s=1$ is always reached as a limit from the right, never through a conditionally convergent series.
nodes.title: Character sums and $L$-values near $s=1$

nodes.summary: For an integer $d$ that is not the square of a rational number (for instance a squarefree $d\ne1$), the field $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$ is a number field of degree $2$. The residue of its Dedekind zeta function at $s=1$ is given by the class number formula, and this section bounds each ingredient of that formula so as to bound the residue from below by $\log\frac{1+\sqrt5}2/(6\sqrt{|d|})$.
